newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke hopes to reduce deficit to 3.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke hopes to reduce deficit to 3.0 pct.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said he hopes to get the budget deficit down to 3.0 precent of GDP in order to put the UK in a position to choose whether or not to join EMU in 1999. "I hope obviously to get our deficit down to 3.0 percent and heading towards balance," he told RFTV in a interview recorded on Sunday and transmitted on Monday.
He said the sixty percent target for the debt-to-GDP ratio is well above where the UK is now, but "I want to start getting that ratio going down soon, long before we get anywhere near 60 percent."

"The Governor of the Bank of England and myself are maintaning monetary policy designed to deliver low, stable inflation so, as I've always said, I expect the British to be in a position where we can make our choice in our interests on whether we want to join (European monetary union)," Clarke said.
But Clarke said the budget deficit still had to be worked at.

"PSBR figures have not tunred out exactly as our people were forecasting. But I think we are at least in as good a position as any other major state to get there. Only Luxembourg is a complete certainty at the moment.

Clarke was speaking after the weekend Ecofin meeting in Dublin. The process towards monetary union took a step forward at the meeting with an agreement, in principle, of a stability pact to enforce greater budgetary discipline among future EMU members. -- Rosemary Bennett +44 171 542 7715
